subject: grayWolf
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: gray wolf standing alert.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm planning a Warcraft-style gray wolf with chunky, exaggerated proportions and painted textures, set on a small snowy rocky base with a pine tree, roughly 1.4m body length and 0.8m shoulder height, making sure the structure stays compatible with the SDK.

Now I'm mapping out the skeleton: hips as the root joint feeding a spine chain forward to the chest, then up through the neck to a raised, alert head position with a jaw joint, plus separate chains for the tail and legs, working out world coordinates for each joint and aim direction along the way.

For the body mesh, I'm deciding to sweep the main torso along the spine path bound to the spine chain of bones, keeping the neck as its own separate sweep rather than merging it into one combined path, since reusing the hips joint across multiple chains risks confusing the binding.

For coloring, I want a painted Warcraft-style coat rather than a flat toon shader -- gray mottled fur on the back, dark saddle patch, cream belly, countershaded by surface normal so the belly lightens where the normal points downward and the back darkens where it points upward.

Now moving to the head: skull as a scaled sphere, snout as a frustum shape, extruded ears, and glowing amber eye decals, each built as separate parts attached to the head bone with their own positions and scales.

Adding small teeth cones and planning a cheek ruff made of spike-shaped fur tufts around the jaw sides.

For the neck ruff, I'm placing two rows of chunky ngon-4 spike shards radially around the neck axis, angled outward and back for a Warcraft-ish fur collar look, parented to the neck's last bone. Now I'm starting on the ears as extruded triangular shapes at the top of the skull.

Working out the eye placement on the skull's ellipsoid surface so the decal sits flush against the curvature, estimating the z-depth from the sphere's scaled radii, and deciding to keep the eye shape symmetric rather than mirroring it separately.

Now I'm adding glow to the eye decals using the glow helper with a strength of 1.2, then moving on to the legs: planning the front leg as a three-segment limb (shoulder, elbow, wrist, paw) with rough joint positions and segment lengths that need to sum to more than the straight-line reach so the limb can bend naturally.

Working out the hind leg geometry with hip and ankle points, choosing knee and hock bend directions, and figuring out how to name the resulting chain of points so each joint and the paw get proper labels for later use.

I'm applying a gradient to the leg fur so the lower legs read lighter than the coat, then shaping paws as flattened spheres positioned at the bone tips so they sit flush with the floor at y=0.

Now I'm adding small dark forward-pointing claw cones to the paw front, bulking up the haunches and shoulders with extra coat-colored spheres near the hip and shoulder joints for a heavier build, and sketching a tail as a curved spline running from the rump downward and back.

For the tail, I'm setting it low and straight for an alert wolf pose, using a four-segment chain tapering from thick to thin, with the tip shaded darker than the body coat -- figuring out whether to use color bands or a gradient paint between the coat color and a dark tip color to get that fade effect.

Now I'm checking body proportions: the chest depth and spine curve need adjusting so the belly sits properly above the ground without legs looking too short, so I'm nudging the spine height and chest radius values to keep things stylized but plausible, then mapping out spine points to shape the curve from shoulder to haunch.

I'm also planning the dorsal mane—a row of spikes running along the back where they'd stand straight up or lean back slightly—and extending the mane up the neck using the same sweep technique.

For the neck, I'm defining a three-point path connecting to the spine's end joint, creating two neck joints parented to the last spine joint, with the head positioned at the top where the path terminates.

Now I'm setting up the head joint parented off the neck, with an aim direction toward the muzzle, plus a jaw joint parented to the head for mouth articulation. The tail gets its own four-joint chain rooted at the hips, while the leg chains split between hips for hind legs and the third spine joint for front legs. I'm about to work out the base setting, possibly a lathed stone disc sized relative to the wolf's overall length.

For the base, I'm deciding on a short cylinder with a snowy top and figuring out how to keep the wolf's feet and the base's lowest point both touching the floor at y=0 -- considering whether to shift the entire wolf model upward by the base height using a coordinate offset helper so everything aligns correctly without manually recalculating every point.

Writing lathe profile and paint function...

I'm adding scene props now: scattered rocks, a pine sapling, a tilted frost rune stone with a glowing cyan texture, and icicle crystals. I'm also giving the wolf a tribal leather collar with bone fang pendant, beads, and a feather, built as a swept loop around the neck.

For the pendant I'll find the front-facing point on the neck collar using an azimuth/elevation lookup, then attach a small bone spike angled downward with a slight forward tilt. Then I want to add tribal war paint markings as a decal along the flank.

Adding fur tufts...

I'm limiting to five texture types total: eye, tuft, rune, claw mark, and ice crystal, applying card clusters to body, tail, neck, and cheek ruff areas. Now I'm designing the eye SVG with an almond amber gradient, dark outline, slit pupil, and slanted brow, mirroring the shape for left and right sides.

Working through the glow decal material and fang/jaw geometry positions, calculating where the upper snout bottom edge and lower jaw top edge meet so the teeth align correctly along the muzzle.

Adding dark fur brow ridges above the eyes and chest ruff tufts pointing down-forward near the neck, plus setting up a reusable tuft helper function for placing these spike clusters.

Now I'm defining the coordinate wrapper for positioning joints along the vertical offset, and checking that the front leg bone lengths reach comfortably between the shoulder root and foot target.

Checking the hind leg similarly: root-to-target distance versus the three segment lengths confirms enough reach, and I'm setting bend directions so the hock joint flexes correctly. For the front leg I'm choosing elbow and wrist bend vectors, then feeding the resulting limb points into the chain builder as a polyline that smooth skinning will round out, and sketching out varying leg radii from shoulder to paw.

Now I'm placing the paw as a scaled sphere at the tip joint with small claw spikes fanned across the front, then adding haunch spheres near the hindquarters for extra body coverage. I'm also setting up the main body sweep along the spine, defining a radius function that interpolates width and height from hips to chest.

I'm sizing the neck radius to taper from the chest and adding ruff spikes at the cheeks and neck to hide the join where the body meets the neck. Then I'm starting on the base props, placing a rune stone as a rotated box with rock-textured material.

Writing stone placement code...

Now I'm designing the pine tree: a trunk with stacked cones for foliage, dusted with smaller white cones on top to look like snow caps, positioned off to the side of the scene.

For ice crystals, I'm scattering a cluster of thin cyan cones leaning at angles with a glow effect, plus a few gray dodecahedron rocks and flattened white sphere snow bumps scattered around. I'm also considering adding a tattered banner pole with red cloth near one of the rune stones for extra flavor, keeping it simple without an emblem.

Writing banner geometry...

Now I'm defining the fur tuft cards for the body, scattering them across the surface with density limits, then adding smaller batches for the neck and tail so coverage tapers naturally across regions.

For the head I'm placing lateral cheek ruff spikes and neck ruff rings using positioned bones, varying direction and length slightly per segment to give a layered mane-like texture around the neck base.

Adding dorsal spikes with dark coloring, then setting up the base paint function: a rocky mottled texture for the body with a lighter frost-blend for areas facing upward.

For the lathe outline, I'm anchoring parts to the hips bone as the static root so rigged bits stay rigid, closing the profile curve properly at both ends. Now I'm defining the skull geometry as a scaled sphere attached to the head bone, positioning it for the eye decal placement.

Placing the eye decal, I realize it overlaps with the snout box at that x/z position, so I'm nudging the eye coordinates outward and upward to clear the collision while adjusting its facing direction accordingly.

Now I'm adding a small dark nose sphere at the snout tip and lowering the snout frustum box slightly, then setting up the tail geometry with a catmull-rom path that feeds a swept chain colored by a gradient transitioning from the coat tone to a darker tip near the end of the tail.

Adding spike and bead geometry for the pendant, then checking placement so the ruff spikes don't obscure the collar — I should position the collar lower around t=0.7 near the neck base so the pendant hangs visibly below the ruff rows, with pendant pointing backward from the front of the neck.

I'm settling on three ruff rows at t .12, .4, .68 with the collar at .85, adjusting radii so spikes sit just above the neck surface without overlap, and coloring by cream in the mid-range of t. Skipping the tongue detail, I estimate the total part count around 150 and move to writing the final geometry.
